_doc: pc/tools/ps1_source_edits.py: K&R variadic functions of the game image whose matched body reads its arguments as consecutive words above its last named parameter (`s32 va_alist; ap = &va_alist;`), which the console's calling convention makes contiguous and x86-64's does not.  The PC build gives them an ANSI `...` prototype and collects the arguments through stdarg, full width (pc/src/ps1_varargs.c); the matched source is not edited.  edits: [old, new(, count)] exact replacements, line count kept.  A stale entry stops the build.  Negative control: test_ps1_source_edits.py VarArgs.

main/sprintf.why: the in-image sprintf (func_800B48D0) walks ap = &va_alist as s32 words; on x86-64 the second variadic argument and the upper half of a pointer are frame garbage. Found by the checkpoint suite (g01_mio, SHOUGATU first meeting): msg_str_disp's %F, sprintf(tmpBuf, msg_str_disp_str7, p_name, pp_name), faulted reading the second %s at 0x20c098ff. %s/%n pointers go through ps1_va_ptr (a sign-extended PS1 address is zero-extended). The words are long long, a pointer's width on LP64 Linux and LLP64 Windows alike (a 32-bit Windows long cut a pointer argument).
